summary: The Playwright tests are syntactically correct and use Playwright APIs properly, so no compile or runtime API errors are detected. All GENERATED test cases (TC-001, TC-002, TC-003) have corresponding tests with preserved testCaseId in titles. Await is correctly used in async assertions. However, selectors are mostly placeholders or weak (e.g., 'text=Product Name', generic 'h1', '.product-description') and URLs with placeholders ('product-detail') weaken navigation validation. The assumption that related products count is 3 may be brittle without data setup. The test design is straightforward but could benefit from more precise selectors and URL validations.

issues.description: Selectors like 'text=Product Name', generic 'h1', and class names such as '.product-description' appear guessed or weak without contextual specificity.
issues.recommendation: Use more robust and unique selectors such as data-testids or ARIA roles to improve test stability and clarity.

issues.description: Navigation confirmation relies on weak URL patterns such as '/product-detail/', which may not sufficiently assert correct product detail page load.
issues.recommendation: Add assertions verifying specific product details or unique identifiers on the page to confirm correct navigation.

issues.description: Product names and URLs are placeholders and may require manual update or test data setup.
issues.recommendation: Replace placeholders with actual test data or parameterize tests to improve reusability.

recommendations: Replace hard-coded placeholder selectors and URLs with actual, stable values from the application under test.
Introduce data-testids or similar custom attributes to improve selector reliability.
Enhance navigation assertions by checking unique page elements or metadata to ensure correct page transition.
Consider parameterizing tests or externalizing test data for greater flexibility and maintainability.
